crm_notes:
Summary: Enterprise quant trading shop evaluating Redwood for latency and unit-cost improvements. POC running since 2026-02-20; focus on batching, KV prefix caching, mixed-precision quantization.

Key requirements:
- 95/99th p99 latency target for inferences: <=50ms for short prompts (<=128 tokens)
- Sustained throughput target: 800-1,200 rps during market open spikes
- Cost target: reduce per-token inference cost by 40% vs current self-hosted fp16 baseline
- Model preference: prefer LlamaX-13B / Falcon variants; open to tuned variants with verified perf profiles
- Routing: regional failover (us-east -> us-west), model-fallback path for degraded capacity
- Data controls: strict residency for trade logs; must support customer-managed KMS and audit logs

Rep notes from 2026-03-05 call:
- "We can tolerate occasional model degradation as long as fallbacks are automatic" (Head of SRE)
- Concern about 8-bit quantization accuracy on reranking step; wants comparison matrix vs int16/fp16
- Interested in Redwood Optimize recommendations: automated batch sizing, cache TTL tuning for prefix-heavy traffic

POC plan and asks:
- Run 24h continuous perf benchmark that simulates market open spikes (bursts to 2k rps for 5 minutes every hour)
- Provide token-level cost breakdown and suggested batching/caching config for their workload
- Deliver quality regression report using their reranking prompt set (50k eval pairs)

Commercial notes:
- Procurement requires SOC2 + ISO27001 certification proof and standard DPA; procurement cycle ~6-8 weeks
- Preliminary ARR range discussed; value prop built on cost reduction and improved tail latency

Open questions:
- Quantization profile recommended for LlamaX-13B with Redwood runtime?
- How will KV cache behave with highly repetitive prefix sequences across sessions?

Short next steps:
- SE to run initial 24h perf run (Daniel)
- Security deep-dive with Rita + security team, provide KMS playbook
- Pricing motion: draft enterprise committed capacity plan for 3-region Dedicated pools
